fact: The Kitchel Lake rules for Phases 1 and 2 of the Second Filing, dated March 1, 2019, carry the same front-sod and 40% non-living lines as the Filing 3 rules.
quote: Astroturf: Astroturf is not allowed in lieu of any required front yard sod requirements. … No more than forty percent (40%) of the front yard landscaping shall be non-living materials, unless otherwise approved by the ACC and the Town of Timnath. The same standard shall apply to back yards.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1 and #3, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Phase 1 and 2, Second Filing (dated March 1, 2019), Astroturf and Landscaping and Irrigation
notes: Read with pdftotext 2026-09-26 from District No. 3's Documents page. The same two lines appear in the Filing 3 rules (timnath-co.kitchel-lake-front-sod, timnath-co.kitchel-lake-nonliving-cap). Neither version names putting greens or defines 'non-living materials'.

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules let the committee require forms and a review fee with a landscaping plan and ask the plan to show the types and locations of fencing, decks, playing areas, sod, seeded areas, edging, retaining walls, rock areas, sprinkler systems, planting beds, mulch areas and landscape lighting.
quote: The ACC may require form(s) to accompany submitted landscaping plans and payment of a review fee (except for the original builder). Plans shall depict types and locations of: fencing, decks, playing areas, sod, seeded areas, edging, retaining walls, rock areas, sprinkler systems, flower beds/gardens, other planting beds, mulch areas, landscape lighting and any other components of the proposed plan.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 37(A) Landscaping and Irrigation
notes: Read with pdftotext 2026-09-26. The list never says putting green; 'playing areas' is the nearest item.

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules ask for three copies of the plan, at least 11 by 17 inches, drawn at one inch to ten feet with a north arrow and showing existing conditions including drainage ways, property lines and easements.
quote: Once an Application submittal has been developed, three (3) copies of a plan (minimum size 11” x 17”) shall be submitted to the Management Company and the ACC. The Application must contain the following information: … C. Scale of one (1) inch – ten (10) feet and north arrow; D. All existing conditions, including house, walks, driveways, patios, decks, walls, plants, trees, drainage ways, property lines, and any easements;
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. IV, No. 5 Applications for Review

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules say that where Town of Timnath standards are more restrictive than the rules, the Town's standards control.
quote: Governmental and Other Regulations. Use of Property and Improvements, as defined in the Covenants, must comply with applicable building codes and other governmental requirements and regulations. Where the provisions of applicable Town of Timnath standards are more restrictive than the provisions of these Rules & Regulations, the Town of Timanth standards shall be controlling.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. III, No. 2 Governmental and Other Regulations
notes: 'Timanth' is the source's own typo. The Phase 1 and 2 rules carry the same section.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1's request form charges a $150 review fee and a $2,500 refundable damage deposit for major improvements such as rear yards, against $50 and $100 for minor landscaping, lets the committee pick the category, issues no approval until the account is paid and refunds the deposit after a post-installation review finds no damage to district property.
quote: Fee and Deposit Schedule … Improvement Type · Review Fee Non-Refundable · Damage Deposit 100% Refundable · Total Due … Paint Change and/or Minor Landscaping: Flower Beds, Fountains, Fencing $50.00 $100.00 $150.00 … Major Improvements: Rear Yards, Pools, New Roof or Siding $150.00 $2500.00 $2,650.00 … ACC to make final determination on improvement type category and will not issue any approvals until the account is paid in full. … No damage to District property from installation, refund of deposit issued
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Application for Modifications or Improvements (ACC request form), Fee and Deposit Schedule and Post Installation Review
notes: Read with pdftotext 2026-09-26 from District No. 1's Covenants and Design Guidelines page (Filing 3); the quote transcribes the fee table row by row. The form carries no revision date. Whether a backyard turf or putting-green request is 'Minor Landscaping' or 'Major Improvements: Rear Yards' is the committee's call, per the form.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 3's design review request lists a $25 review fee for each submittal, asks for drawings to scale showing placement, materials and dimensions, and says processing may take up to 30 days.
quote: Please review your architectural guidelines and submit detailed drawing(s) to scale showing placement, materials, and dimensions. Incomplete submissions will not be reviewed and will delay the approval of your application. It may take upto 30 days for your application to be processed and approved.* … Please note: A $25 review fee applies to each submittal.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 3, Design Review Request form (linked from the district's Architectural Review page)
notes: Read with pdftotext 2026-09-26. District No. 3's Architectural Review page also names a $25.00 fee. An older District No. 3 page (/covenants-and-design-guidelines) still mentions a '$50 Review Fee which is paid at closing' and the former manager; the current page and form say $25, so pages use $25 and send owners to the district.

fact: The Kitchel Lake declaration recorded July 17, 2020 has the Architectural Control Committee approve or disapprove a request within 30 days after a complete submission and treats a failure to approve within 30 days as disapproval.
quote: The ACC shall approve or disapprove all requests for approval within thirty (30) days after the complete submission of all plans, specifications, and other materials and information which the ACC may require in conjunction therewith. … Failure to approve the plans and specifications within thirty (30) days shall be deemed disapproval.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake, recorded July 17, 2020 (Larimer County Reception No. 20200053169), Section 2.5
notes: Read with pdftotext 2026-09-26. The same recording is also posted by District No. 3 as CC&Rs_Recorded_200717.pdf. Its Exhibit A covers Blocks 6, 7, 9, 11 and 17-24 of the Second Filing (see decl-2020-blocks).

fact: Filing 3's own Kitchel Lake declaration, recorded in April 2023 with Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1 as its district, gives the committee the same 30 days after a complete submission and treats a failure to approve within them as disapproval.
quote: The ACC shall approve or disapprove all requests for approval within thirty (30) days after the complete submission of all plans, specifications, and other materials and information which the ACC may require in conjunction therewith. … Failure to approve the plans and specifications within thirty (30) days shall be deemed disapproval.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake (Kitchel Lake F3 Development Corporation), recorded April 7, 2023 and re-recorded April 13, 2023 (Larimer County Reception No. 20230014455), Section 2.5
notes: The PDF is a scan with no text layer; Section 2.5 read from the page image (page 7 of 27) 2026-09-26. Re-recorded to add a missing consent signature page.

fact: The 2020 Kitchel Lake declaration lets an applicant appeal an adverse committee decision to the district board in writing within 10 days and treats approved work not finished within one year as unapproved unless the committee extends the time.
quote: In the event the ACC decides a request for architectural approval which is adverse to the applicant, then the applicant shall have the right to an appeal of such decision to the full Governing Board, if different than the ACC, upon a written request therefor submitted to the Governing Board within ten (10) days after such decision by the ACC. … Failure to complete the proposed Improvement within one (1) year after the date of approval of the application or to complete the Improvement in complete conformance with the conditions and requirements of the approval, shall constitute noncompliance with the requirement that approval for Improvements be obtained from the ACC; provided, however, the ACC, in its discretion, may grant extensions of time for completion of any proposed Improvements.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake, recorded July 17, 2020 (Larimer County Reception No. 20200053169), Sections 2.6 and 2.7
notes: The OCR text layer reads 'one (I) year'; the page reads 'one (1) year'. Filing 3's declaration carries the same Sections 2.6 and 2.7 (page 7 image).

fact: The 2020 Kitchel Lake declaration gives the person responsible 45 days after a notice of noncompliance to remedy or remove the work, after which the committee may remove it or record a notice against the lot and bill the costs.
quote: If the ACC determines that a noncompliance exists, the Person responsible for such noncompliance shall remedy or remove the same (and return the subject real estate and/or Improvements or structure to its original condition) within a period of not more than forty-five (45) days from the date of receipt of the notice of noncompliance. If such Person does not comply with the ruling within such period, the ACC may, at its option, record a notice of noncompliance against the Lot on which the noncompliance exists, may remove the non-complying Improvement or may otherwise remedy the noncompliance, and the Person responsible for such noncompliance shall reimburse the ACC, upon demand, for all costs and expenses incurred with respect thereto.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake, recorded July 17, 2020 (Larimer County Reception No. 20200053169), Section 2.11

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 fine schedule starts with a warning, then fines of $25, $50 and $50 every two weeks for work that needed committee approval, and $25, $100 and then $200 every two weeks for work that doesn't match its approval.
quote: Architectural Committee Review and Approval Required · Warning · $25 · $50 · $50 · Bi-weekly … Architectural Review, Improvement not Conforming to Request/Approval · Warning · $25 · $100 · $200 · Bi-weekly
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Attachment B, Schedule of Fines
notes: Table columns: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, Thereafter, Assess. The quote joins the table cells with middle dots.

fact: The 2020 Kitchel Lake declaration says it does not create a common interest community under the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act and is not governed by that act.
quote: WHEREAS, this Declaration does not create a Common Interest Community, as defined by the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act at C.R.S. §38-33.3-103(8), as amended; therefore, this Declaration shall not be governed by the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act or any provisions thereof.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake, recorded July 17, 2020 (Larimer County Reception No. 20200053169), Recitals
notes: What this means for the state backyard-turf statutes is a legal question; pages state the recital and point to the Colorado rule band, and do not conclude.

fact: Filing 3's Kitchel Lake declaration, recorded in 2023, also says it does not create a common interest community under the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act.
quote: WHEREAS, this Declaration does not create a Common Interest Community, as defined by the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act at C.R.S. §38-33.3-103(8), as amended; therefore, this Declaration shall not be governed by the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act or any provisions thereof.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake (Kitchel Lake F3 Development Corporation), re-recorded April 13, 2023 (Larimer County Reception No. 20230014455), Recitals
notes: Read from the page image (page 2 of 27), 2026-09-26.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1 describes itself as a quasi-municipal corporation organized under the Colorado Special District Act, formed in May 2006 and covering about 177.3 acres east of Interstate 25 and north of Prospect Road.
quote: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1 (SFMD #1) is a quasi-municipal corporation organized and operated pursuant to the provisions set forth in the Colorado Special District Act, and was formed in May 2006. The District was established as part of a “Multiple District Structure” for the community located in the Town of Timnath, Larimer County, Colorado and is approximately 177.3 acres generally located East of Interstate 25 and Larimer County Road 5, North of Prospect Road (Larimer County Road 44), West of Larimer County Road 3, and South of Colorado Highway #14.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1, 2025 Annual Report (submitted July 27, 2026), Exhibit A, 2026 Budget Message

fact: Filing 3's Kitchel Lake declaration bars owners and their contractors from using open space next to a lot as construction access, or for any access other than on foot, without the committee's or the district board's express written consent, and makes the owner answer for any damage plus fines.
quote: At no time, without express written consent of the ACC or Governing Board, are Owners, their contractors, or any representative of the Owner, permitted to use open space abutting the Owner’s property as construction access or for any access other than pedestrian. Any damage caused to the property may be repaired by the Governing Board and the Owner will be solely responsible for such damages, in addition to any fines and fees places on the owner for this violation as permitted by the Governing Board.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake (Kitchel Lake F3 Development Corporation), re-recorded April 13, 2023 (Larimer County Reception No. 20230014455), Section 3.14 Lot Access
notes: Read from the page image (page 14 of 27), 2026-09-26; 'fees places' is the source's own wording. The 2020 declaration for part of the Second Filing has no Lot Access section (its 3.14 is grade and drainage).

fact: The Kitchel Lake declaration recorded July 17, 2020 covers Blocks 6, 7, 9, 11 and 17 through 24 of the Serratoga Falls Second Filing.
quote: Lots 1 through 3, inclusive, Block 6, Lots 1 through 4, inclusive, Block 7, Lots 1 through 11, inclusive, Block 9, Lots 1 through 12, inclusive, Block 11, Lots 1 through 12, inclusive, Block 17, Lots 1 through 3, inclusive, Block 18, Lots 1 through 7, inclusive, Block 19, Lots 1 through 8, inclusive, Block 20, Lots 1 through 16, inclusive, Block 21, Lots 1 through 16, inclusive, Block 22, Lots 1 through 6, inclusive, Block 23, Lots 1 through 12, inclusive, Block 24, All in Serratoga Falls -- Second Filing, County of Larimer, State of Colorado.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1 posts a boundary map for owners to tell whether their lot is in District No. 1 or District No. 3.
quote: The Boundary Map can be seen here to identify if you are in District 1 or 3.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1, How to Identify your District (web page, with the SF D1 & D3 Boundary Map)

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules hold fences to the community standard of 4 feet with three rails, require the community fence wherever a lot adjoins common area, and allow wire mesh for pets with committee approval.
quote: Fencing is allowed only in accordance with the community standard, which is a maximum height of four (4) feet (not including columns) with three (3) rails, as shown below: … The Community fence must be installed in any portion of the Lot which adjoins common area, per the approved Fencing Plan for Kitchel Lake. … Upon review and approval by the ACC, installation of wire mesh to the three (3) rail fence may be allowed for pet containment purposes.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 26 Fences

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules let the rear 10-foot utility easement sit inside the back-yard fence but keep it open to utility company and district access, and warn that utilities may remove a fence in an easement with no duty to restore it.
quote: Owners are advised that various utility companies and other service vendors may have the right to access the Lot because of established easements (including removal of fence with no obligation to restore). … The rear 10’ utility easement may be enclosed in the rear yard fencing, but is subject to utility company and District access per note C above.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 26(C) and (F) Fences

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1's request form makes the owner responsible for damage to infrastructure in an easement and for replacing their own improvements there when someone else's use of the easement disturbs them.
quote: In regards to improvements made within any easements; I fully understand that I am responsible for any damages caused to existing infrastructure within the easement, and any future costs or implications associated with future use of the easement, including any replacement costs of my installed improvements caused by another’s use and product placement within the easement.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Application for Modifications or Improvements (ACC request form), owner acknowledgments

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1's request form says committee approval is not approval from the local building or zoning department and is withdrawn if a required permit or approval isn't obtained.
quote: ACC approval does not constitute approval of the local building or zoning department, drainage design, structural or engineering safety and/or soundness. I understand that I may be required to obtain building or other permits prior to the commencement of any work. I agree that my failure to obtain required building or other permits/approvals will result in the withdrawal of ACC approval.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Application for Modifications or Improvements (ACC request form), owner acknowledgments

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1's irrigation start-up guide puts two irrigation boxes along the rear of each property, a valve box with a blowout port and a meter box that is district property homeowners and contractors must not tamper with.
quote: Each residence has two irrigation boxes along the rear of each property. There is a valve box that contains a blowout port and ball valve (see “Picture A” below; this box may also be round). Each residence also has a dedicated meter box (see “Picture B” below). … The meter box in “Picture B” is metro district property and should not be tampered with by homeowners or contractors.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metro District No. 1, Start up Instructions & Irrigation Water Schedule (Residential Irrigation Start-Up Guide, posted with the April 30, 2026 irrigation letter)
notes: District No. 3's 2024 guide describes its lots differently: a green valve box inside the back property line and the tap and meter on the district side of the back fence.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1 holds homes to a three-day-a-week watering schedule in four-hour night windows set by address, and requires owners who need extra water for a landscape installation to ask the district's permission, ideally before the work.
quote: The District currently follows a strict three (3) day per week watering schedule for all homes. The schedule for your property varies by address: · Even Last Number Preceded by Odd Number: Monday, Wednesday, Friday – 10 p.m. to 2 a.m. … · Odd Last Number Preceded by Even Number: Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday – 2 a.m. to 6 a.m. … If you need additional watering time due to landscape installations, it is required that the homeowner request permission for additional water from the District. It would be appreciated if the request was made ahead of the landcape installation so that water availability and timing may be considered prior to permission being granted.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1, Watering Schedule (web page)
notes: District No. 3's Watering Schedule page lists the same four address windows.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1's 2023 water rules cover only the irrigation system, leave drinking water to ELCO, and set the irrigation season as May 1 through October 15 unless the district decides otherwise.
quote: These Rules and Regulations apply only to the Irrigation Water System (as defined herein); not to the potable water system, as that will be managed and controlled by East Larimer County Water District (“ELCO”). … Unless otherwise determined by the District, the Irrigation Season shall be the period of May 1 through October 15.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1, Water Rules and Regulations (adopted March 30, 2023), Sections 1.2 and 8.6

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1's 2023 water rules allow special permits for special circumstances, including watering new sod.
quote: Special Permits may be issued to allow for special circumstances, including sod watering
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1, Water Rules and Regulations (adopted March 30, 2023), Appendix B, Watering Schedule, Irrigation Water System – Restrictions of Use

fact: On April 30, 2026, the district told Serratoga residents that after a historically dry winter and spring the reservoir was too low to start the master irrigation pumping station, that well water would go first to trees and shrubs, and that broader residential watering was targeted for May 18.
quote: We are entering a challenging irrigation season following an historically dry winter and spring. … At this time, the current target date for more comprehensive residential watering is May 18, depending on reservoir water levels and available water supply. … The reservoir water level remains too low to start the master irrigation pumping station. … For the next two to three weeks, available well water will be used for targeted irrigation of high-value plant material, including trees and shrubs throughout the community.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metro District No. 1, irrigation letter to Serratoga residents, April 30, 2026
notes: Page 1 of the district's start-up PDF. Recheck against the next season's start-up letter.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 3's 2024 start-up letter billed irrigation water by use at $3.92 per 1,000 gallons with a $25 monthly minimum, capped seasonal use at 93,000 gallons with a $250 surcharge for overages, and dropped the xeriscape discount.
quote: The water rates will now be billed based on usage as follows: • $3.92 per 1,000 gallons with a minimum monthly charge (not a base charge) of $25.00 during irrigation season. • Maximum seasonal usage of 93,000 gallons. Seasonal overages will result in a $250 surcharge. • There will be no xeriscape discount for 2024 since the District is moving to metered usage.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metro District No. 3, 2024 Non-Potable Water Startup letter (April 23, 2024)
notes: The newest rate notice District No. 3 posts; 2025 and 2026 rates were not found on its site, so pages date these as 2024. The 2021 water rules it replaced gave rear-yard xeriscapes a 15% flat-fee reduction.

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules require sprinkler systems to irrigate the landscaping in the front lawn.
quote: Sprinkler systems must be installed to irrigate landscaping in the front lawn. The semi-arid climate makes watering necessary.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 37(A) Landscaping and Irrigation

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules require owners beside a street tree lawn to plant and maintain grass or a groundcover of a type the committee approves there, watered by an underground sprinkler system bored under the sidewalk.
quote: Owners of a Lot must maintain the builder installed tree(s) required by the Town of Timnath. Owners of a Lot adjacent to a street tree lawn are required to plant and maintain grass or groundcover of a type approved by the ACC in the adjacent street tree lawn abutting the Lot and shall install (including boring under the sidewalk) and maintain an underground sprinkler system.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 37(A) Landscaping and Irrigation

fact: The 2020 Kitchel Lake declaration defines a lot's established drainage as the grading plan the Town of Timnath approved and requires a committee-approved plan before any change to it.
quote: Each Owner agrees that the Owner will not in any way interfere with the established drainage pattern over the Owner's Lot. In the event that it is necessary or desirable to change the established drainage over any Lot, then the Owner thereof shall submit a plan to the ACC for its review and approval, in accordance with the provisions of Article 2 of this Declaration and any such change shall also be made in accordance with all laws, regulations and resolutions of any applicable governmental entities. … For purposes of this Section, "established drainage" is defined as the Grading Plan approved by the Town of Timnath, provided by the Project Engineer.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, Restrictions and Easements for Kitchel Lake, recorded July 17, 2020 (Larimer County Reception No. 20200053169), Section 3.14.1
notes: Filing 3's declaration carries the same text as Section 3.15.1 (page 14 image).

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules say landscaping should follow the established drainage pattern, that a drainage engineer's report may be required with an application, and that the lot causing harm to a neighbor must correct it.
quote: When performing any landscaping work or performing any work to maintain the established drainage pattern, it is very important to insure that water drains away from the foundation of the house into the street and that the flow patterns prevent water from flowing under or against the house foundation, walkways, sidewalks, and driveways. A report may be required from a drainage engineer as part of the Application. Landscaping should conform to the established drainage pattern. … Adverse effects to adjacent properties will not be tolerated and correction of such will be the responsibility of the offending Lot.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 22 Drainage/Grading & Grade Changes

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules need approval for decks, limit a deck to 25% of the rear lot and set it at least 5 feet from the property line.
quote: Decks & Balconies: Approval is required. … Decks may not be more than twenty-five percent (25%) of the entire rear Lot of the home. Construction shall not occur over easements beyond the side plane of the home and must be set back a minimum of five (5) feet from the Property line.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 19 Decks & Balconies

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules recommend keeping regularly watered beds and sprinkler piping and heads at least 5 feet from foundation walls and slabs.
quote: It is recommended that flower beds (especially annuals), vegetable gardens and other landscaping which requires regular watering, should not be planted within five (5) feet of the foundation wall or slab and should avoid excessive watering. Further, piping and heads for sprinkler systems should not be installed within five (5) feet of foundation walls and slabs.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 30 Gardens

fact: Kitchel Lake's Filing 3 rules bar an accessory building from blocking another owner's direct view of the mountains or the lake and require a masonry wrap on every rear elevation that faces the Kitchell Reservoir.
quote: Accessory buildings shall not obstruct another Lot Owner’s direct view of mountains or lake. … Masonry corners need to wrap a minimum of 4’. … Required for all rear elevations that face of street, roadway, or Kitchell Reservoir.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District #1, Rules and Regulations, Kitchel Lake, Filing 3 (adopted March 30, 2023), Art. V, No. 1(C) and Art. VI, No. 7(B)
notes: The community is spelled Kitchel; the reservoir, in these rules and the service plan, Kitchell.

fact: The 2006 consolidated service plan for the Serratoga Falls metro districts covers about 388.26 acres and draws part of the boundary along the high-water line of the Kitchell Reservoir, previously known as the Kitchell & Moore Reservoir, at elevation 4959.50.
quote: The area of the Districts Boundaries includes approximately three hundred eighty-eight and twenty-six one hundredths (388.26) acres. … ALSO BEING A POINT ON A LINE BEING THE HIGH WATER LINE OF "THE KITCHELL RESERVOIR", PREVIOUSLY KNOW AS "THE KITCHELL & MOORE RESERVOIR", AS SAID RESERVOIR COVERS WHEN THE WATER IS UP TO SIX AND ONE-HALF (6 1/2) FEET ABOVE THE GRADE OF THE OUTLET DITCH OF SAID RESERVOIR. THE ELEVATION OF SAID LINE BEING 4959.50 BASED UPON THE NAVD 1988 DATUM;
source_label: Consolidated Service Plan for Serratoga Falls Metropolitan Districts (approved by the Town of Timnath March 29, 2006), Section III and Exhibit A legal description
notes: 'PREVIOUSLY KNOW AS' is the source's own wording. The plan was amended and restated in 2016 and amended in 2021 (per the 2023 Filing 3 declaration's recitals).

fact: Larimer County's platted-lot map draws 500 numbered lots across Serratoga Falls' Second Filing, Third Filing and Third Filing replat, 430 of them between 6,500 and 13,000 square feet, with a median of about 8,500 and 136 at 10,000 or more.
quote: SUBNAME: SERRATOGA FALLS 2ND (SUBNUM 5010002000) · SERRATOGA FALLS 3RD (SUBNUM 5010003000) · SERRATOGA FALLS 3RD REPLAT (SUBNUM 5010003001) · LABEL: numbered lots and lettered tracts
source_label: Larimer County parcel GIS, Platted Lots layer: Serratoga Falls 2nd, 3rd and 3rd Replat, lot areas computed from the lot polygons
notes: Query UPPER(SUBNAME) LIKE '%SERRATOGA%', outSR 2231 (Colorado North State Plane, US feet); shoelace area of each numbered lot polygon. Second Filing 250 lots (matches the 140 + 110 lots of the 2018 and 2020 declarations), Third 206, Third Replat 44 (no overlap with the Third). fact: Trumark Homes describes 65-foot homesites throughout Kitchel Lake and says the community will feature a clubhouse, water access and open space.
quote: Spacious 65-foot homesites throughout the community … The community will feature a clubhouse, water access, and vast open space, making it an ideal place for relaxation and recreation.
source_label: Trumark Homes, Kitchel Lake at Serratoga Falls (community page)
notes: A builder's marketing page; pages use only the homesite width and the planned amenities, never its prices or floor plans.

fact: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1 reported in July 2026 that the Town approved the site plan for a clubhouse and pool, with construction to start once the Town gives final approval, and that a pocket park and a playground are expected by the end of 2026.
quote: Landscaping is also substantially complete throughout Phases 1 through 4, except for the installation of one pocket park and one playground, both of which are expected to be completed before the end of 2026. The Town has approved the site plan for a clubhouse and pool at the development. The clubhouse building plans remain under Town review, and construction of the clubhouse and pool project is expected to begin once the Town provides final approval.
source_label: Serratoga Falls Metropolitan District No. 1, 2025 Annual Report (submitted July 27, 2026), item 5
notes: Phases 1 through 4 are Filing 3's. Recheck against the 2026 annual report.
